title: Exam F3FIE: Risk Management
name: Risk Management
source_title: FCIA Syllabus – Finance, investments and ERM with option in Banking
intro: The aim of this exam is for candidates to develop the following skills:
1. Understand the main principles and techniques of enterprise risk management (ERM) and economic capital modelling that are relevant to life insurance.
2. Apply these principles and techniques within the context of investments.
3. Understand how ERM and economic capital modelling links to wider business processes (e.g., business planning, pricing, and capital setting).
4. Create and evaluate hypothetical scenarios, including using judgement to assess the implications of possible actions and to develop appropriate investment proposals or recommendations.

Exams are administered as an open-book, four-hour exam requiring analysis in the context of a problem and written responses to specific questions. Candidates will complete the exam through the CIA learning management system.

Apply the concept of ERM. (D3)
Apply the framework for risk management and control within an insurer. (D3)
Describe regulatory requirements related to ERM including own-risk and solvency assessment. (A2)
Describe the perspectives of credit-rating agencies. (B2)
Reflect data issues in general and special considerations with respect to ERM. (C3)

topics.title: Economic capital modelling and aggregation of risks

bullets: a. Describe enterprise-wide risk aggregation techniques that incorporate the use of correlation. (C2)

bullets: a. Describe the development and use of models for decision-making purposes in ERM. (B2)

b. Demonstrate how the decision-making process considers the organization’s risk appetite and corporate governance, and builds on the results of stochastic modelling, scenario analysis, stress testing, and analysis of model and parameter risk. (D4)

Calculate regulatory capital requirement. (C3)

Describe the Appointed Actuary’s responsibilities related to financial condition testing (FCT). (A2)
